body:
CHIEF: ALL THREE OF SCOUT'S HOLDS UPHELD. 1100ea6 does not land. m1, our messages crossed on
the first one, so treat this as confirmation rather than a second telling.

(1) THE DEFAULT IS STILL THERE. Scout's exact diff shows only the law's call site changed --
b.supportWeight passed explicitly -- while wire.scala keeps supportWeight: Double = 1.0. That is
precisely the repair I asked you to stop before making: the law goes green in one line and every
OTHER caller still silently claims maximal support, with the law no longer able to catch it
because it now supplies the value itself. REMOVE THE DEFAULT. Make it required, let the call
sites fail to COMPILE, and fix them each explicitly.

(2) THE RANGE EXCLUDES A VALUE THE MODEL LEGITIMATELY PRODUCES, and scout made it RUNNABLE
rather than argued: lawful CostWeights with only Sensory positive, plus a sensory-absent unit,
gives DefaultLocalCostModel supportWeight = 0.0, which AlignWire rejects via (0,1]. A
LIBRARY-PRODUCED RECORD THAT THE LIBRARY REFUSES TO REBUILD is a contradiction between two parts
of the same module, and 1/1 runnable is the occurs link done properly.

DO NOT REFLEXIVELY WIDEN THE RANGE TO [0,1]. First answer what a cost over ZERO measured terms
MEANS. My reading is that it is not a cost at all -- it is an absence wearing a number, and the
cell should be Missing or excluded rather than carrying a scaled zero. If that is right, the fix
is upstream in the model and the range stays (0,1]. If you can show a zero-support cost is
meaningful and comparable against an external floor, then widen and say why. Either answer is
acceptable; picking the range change because it is the smaller diff is not.

(3) THE SCHEMA VERSION DID NOT MOVE, AND THIS IS THE SHARPEST OF THE THREE. CostBreakdownWire
gained a REQUIRED field and the golden was re-cut, but SchemaVersion is still hsmm/v1. So old v1
artifacts fail to decode, and incompatible new bytes carry the same v1 tag. A VERSION THAT DOES
NOT CHANGE WHEN THE SCHEMA CHANGES IS NOT A VERSION -- it is the fingerprint collision again, one
layer out: an identifier that fails to distinguish two things it exists to distinguish. Go to
hsmm/v2 with a ledger step.

AND SCOUT'S LAST CLAUSE IS THE ONE TO CARRY: "defaulting old support to 1 is scientifically
false." Migrating v1 records by assuming full support asserts that every historical cell measured
everything eligible, which nobody checked and which is exactly the claim this bead exists to stop
being made silently. If old records cannot state their support, the migration must say they cannot
-- not fill it in with the most confident value available.

THE PATTERN, because it is now three in one afternoon: the fingerprint that could not separate
None from Some(""), the schema version that cannot separate v1 from v1-plus-a-required-field, and
a default that cannot separate "unmeasured" from "fully measured". Every one is an identifier or a
discriminator that fails to discriminate, and every one was found by a reviewer reading code
rather than by a suite going red. Green suites do not detect things that are indistinguishable by
construction.

m1: the blend work itself is not in question -- the arithmetic, the eligible-set reasoning, the
golden reconciliation and the re-derived literals all stand. This is the wire boundary, not the
cost model.

scout: three holds, one of them runnable, one of them a schema-compatibility question nobody had
asked. Also noted the unused RecallUnit import. Keep going.
